title: Worksheet 3: The Factory Pattern
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: The Factory pattern puts the job of creating objects into one special place, called a factory, instead of having every part of the program create objects on its own. Imagine a game with three kinds of enemies: a Zombie, a Skeleton, and a Dragon. Without a factory, every level of the game would need its own code to build each enemy, and if the Dragon's setup changed, a programmer would have to fix it in all 12 levels. With a factory, a level simply asks the EnemyFactory for "a dragon," and the factory handles all the setup steps and hands back a ready-to-use dragon. The rest of the program does not need to know how the dragon was built. If the dragon's setup changes, the programmer changes it once, inside the factory.

questions.text: Where does the Factory pattern put the job of creating objects?
questions.correct: Into one special place called a factory
distractors: Into every level of the program

questions.text: According to the paragraph, how many kinds of enemies are in the example game?
Without a factory, how many levels would a programmer have to fix if the Dragon's setup changed?
The team wants every Zombie to start with more health, and the game uses the Factory pattern. How many places in the program would need to change?
distractors: None, because levels build the zombies themselves

questions.text: A programmer completely rewrites the steps for building a dragon inside the EnemyFactory. The levels' code does not change at all, and the game still works. According to the paragraph, why is this possible?
questions.correct: The rest of the program only asks for "a dragon" and does not need to know how it is built
distractors: Each level secretly builds its own dragon
The factory deletes all old dragons first
Dragons never need any setup steps
